section: Biotechnology - nature, scope, tools; applications in agriculture, medicine and industry
subsections: Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes

accepted.s: Which of the following most appropriately describes bioremediation?
o: Thermal destruction of contaminated soil by incineration
Removal or degradation of pollutants by organisms or their enzymes
Physical excavation and permanent burial of contaminated material
Chemical conversion of all pollutants into radioactive substances
accepted.x: Bioremediation uses organisms such as bacteria, fungi, algae and plants, or their enzymes, to degrade or remove pollutants and restore a contaminated environment.
accepted.tq: Use the exact definition and distinguish biological treatment from thermal or physical treatment.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bioventing — injection of air below the water table
Biosparging — supply of air or nutrients through wells
Landfarming — treatment in a slurry bioreactor
accepted.x: Bioaugmentation involves adding microorganisms to enhance contaminant degradation. Bioventing supplies air or nutrients through wells, whereas biosparging injects air below the water table.
accepted.tq: Match each technique with its defining operation before eliminating swapped descriptions.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding bioremediation techniques:
1. Bioventing supplies air or nutrients through wells.
2. Biosparging involves injection of air below the water table.
3. Landfarming is an ex-situ technique.
4. Slurry and aqueous reactors are generally the fastest and costliest bioremediation systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Bioventing and biosparging are in-situ methods, landfarming is ex-situ, and bioreactors are described as the fastest but costliest systems.
accepted.tq: Split the statements by category and verify the location, operation and performance of each technique.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following sets contains only ex-situ bioremediation techniques?
accepted.x: Landfarming, composting and biopiles require contaminated material to be treated outside its original location and are ex-situ techniques.
accepted.tq: Classify the techniques by whether the contaminated material remains at the site.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A contaminated site is treated without excavating the polluted material, using a passive and relatively cheaper method. This approach is known as:
accepted.x: In-situ bioremediation treats contamination at its original site and is generally cheaper and more passive than ex-situ treatment.
accepted.tq: Apply the site-treatment condition first: treatment at the original location indicates in-situ remediation.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Approach)
A. Phytoremediation
B. Mycoremediation
C. Rhizoremediation
D. Bioaugmentation

List-II (Agent or basis)
1. Fungi
2. Added microorganisms
3. Plants
4. Microorganisms associated with plant roots

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Phytoremediation uses plants, mycoremediation uses fungi, rhizoremediation uses root-zone microbes, and bioaugmentation adds microorganisms.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pairs based on the prefixes phyto-, myco- and rhizo-.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Water hyacinth — phytoextraction of heavy metals
Eucalyptus along sewage ponds — arsenite degradation by bacteria
Ideonella sakaiensis — removal of arsenate from groundwater
Bacillus flexus — degradation of PET plastic
accepted.x: Water hyacinth can be used in phytoextraction of heavy metals, while eucalyptus has been associated with sewage ponds. Ideonella sakaiensis degrades PET plastic and Bacillus flexus is associated with arsenate removal.
accepted.tq: Use the pollutant-agent association and reject the options that swap biological agents.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bacillus flexus is associated with the removal of arsenate.
2. Acinetobacter junii is associated with the removal of arsenite.
3. Ideonella sakaiensis degrades PET plastic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Bacillus flexus is associated with arsenate removal, Acinetobacter junii with arsenite removal, and Ideonella sakaiensis with PET degradation.
accepted.tq: Check each named microbe against its specific pollutant rather than treating all microbial remediation as interchangeable.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with an application of bioremediation?
o: Oil spills — bioaugmentation with oil-degrading bacteria
Heavy metals — exclusive use of algal blooms
Sewage drains — burning of contaminated soil
accepted.x: Oil spills and oily sludge may be treated through bioaugmentation with oil-degrading bacteria. The other options describe harmful processes or unsuitable treatments.
accepted.tq: Match the pollutant with its biological treatment route and reject reversed ecological processes.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Indian applications of bioremediation, consider the following statements:
1. TERI has used a consortium for oil-spill treatment at Chennai port.
2. CPCB has undertaken bioremediation of oil-contaminated soils.
3. CSIR-NEERI has developed technology for heavy-metal removal from industrial effluents.
4. Legacy municipal waste can be addressed through biomining along with bioremediation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The examples include TERI's Chennai port work, CPCB treatment of oil-contaminated soils, CSIR-NEERI heavy-metal technology and biomining of legacy waste.
accepted.tq: Treat each institutional example as a separate statement and check the agency, pollutant and application.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which organisation is identified as the nodal research and development body for bioremediation in India?
accepted.x: CSIR-NEERI is identified as the nodal R&D body for bioremediation in India. TERI and CPCB are associated with particular applications, while IOCL is linked with biofuel initiatives.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-role distinction: nodal R&D body is different from an implementing or industrial organisation.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Arsenic contamination — exclusive treatment through PET-degrading bacteria
Legacy municipal waste — biomining plus bioremediation
Mine waste and tailings — long-term effluent-treatment monitoring
Sewage and lakes — biostimulation, aquatic plants and constructed wetlands
accepted.x: Arsenic contamination is associated with resistant bacteria such as Bacillus flexus and Acinetobacter junii, not PET-degrading bacteria. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the pollutant-treatment mismatch by identifying the option that uses an unrelated microbial function.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes biomagnification from bioremediation?
o: Biomagnification is the rise of persistent toxins up a food chain, whereas bioremediation degrades or removes pollutants.
Bioremediation increases DDT concentration at successive trophic levels.
Biomagnification is a method of treating oil spills with bacteria.
Both terms refer to the biological removal of pollutants from soil.
accepted.x: Biomagnification is the increasing concentration of persistent toxins such as DDT or mercury along a food chain. Bioremediation is the biological degradation or removal of pollutants.
accepted.tq: Separate similar-looking biological terms by their direction of effect: pollutant increase versus pollutant removal.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding bioremediation is correct?
o: It can address oil spills, heavy metals, pesticides, solvents and organic pollutants.
It is restricted to soil and cannot be applied to water or air.
It always requires excavation of contaminated material.
accepted.x: Bioremediation can be applied to soil, water and air and may address oil spills, heavy metals, pesticides, solvents and other organic pollutants. It may be in-situ or ex-situ, and engineered microbes can be used.
accepted.tq: Test the scope of the process across media, pollutants and treatment conditions.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of relative speed and cost for bioreactors as described in environmental biotechnology?
accepted.x: Slurry and aqueous bioreactors are described as the fastest bioremediation systems, but they are also the costliest.
accepted.tq: Read the paired comparison carefully; both descriptors must be retained rather than selecting only speed or cost.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about genetically modified microbes and plants is correct?
o: They can be designed to reduce pollution and conserve resources.
They are restricted to medical applications.
They are used only for increasing biomagnification.
They cannot degrade oil or plastic.
accepted.x: Biotechnology uses genetically modified microbes and plants for pollution reduction and resource conservation, including oil degradation and plastic breakdown.
accepted.tq: Apply the stated role of genetic engineering to environmental problems rather than limiting it to medicine.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Engineered Pseudomonas and algae — oil-spill treatment
2. PETase-producing bacteria — plastic degradation
3. PLA and PHA — bioplastics from engineered microbes
4. Biofilters — microbe-laden beds for pollutants in air and gas streams
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Engineered Pseudomonas and algae can target oil spills, PETase-producing bacteria break down plastic, engineered microbes can produce PLA and PHA, and biofilters use microbe-laden beds to treat air or gas streams.
accepted.tq: Verify each tool by its product or environmental application; the comprehensive option is justified when all pairs align.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Pilot plants for producing bioplastics such as PLA and PHA from engineered microbes are mentioned in:
accepted.x: Pilot plants for microbial production of the bioplastics PLA and PHA are mentioned in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.
accepted.tq: Use the location-product association and distinguish bioplastics sites from waste-to-energy locations.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: 2G ethanol from crop residue — IOCL Panipat
Municipal waste to CNG — Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu pilot plants only
E20 blending target — Hyderabad and Pune waste-to-CNG plants
accepted.x: IOCL Panipat is associated with 2G ethanol production from crop residue. Gobar-Dhan concerns biogas, municipal waste-to-CNG is associated with Hyderabad and Pune, and Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu are linked with bioplastics pilot plants.
accepted.tq: Match each technology with its feedstock or location, watching for swapped examples.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The E20 blending target referred to in the context of biofuels is associated with which period?
accepted.x: The E20 blending target is associated with the period 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Check the year range precisely; nearby-year options are designed to test date retention.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following applications in the order in which they are associated with the relevant technologies listed:
A. Gobar-Dhan — biogas
B. PETase-producing bacteria — plastic degradation
C. IOCL Panipat — 2G ethanol from crop residue
D. Biofilters — treatment of pollutants in air and gas streams
Which of the following is the correct order from bioenergy to pollution-treatment applications?
accepted.x: The sequence follows the listed progression from Gobar-Dhan biogas, to 2G ethanol at IOCL Panipat, to PET degradation, and finally biofilters for air and gas streams.
accepted.tq: Use the functional sequence from bioenergy production to plastic and air-pollutant treatment.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The BioE3 policy was approved by the Union Cabinet in:
accepted.x: The BioE3 policy, meaning Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment, was approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2024.
accepted.tq: Retain the exact approval month and year instead of relying only on the policy acronym.
accepted.sec: ■ Environmental biotechnology - bioremediation types, GM microbes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is identified as a key thematic area of the BioE3 policy?
o: Restriction of biotechnology to pharmaceutical imports
Replacement of all biological treatment by incineration
accepted.x: Climate-resilient agriculture is identified as a key thematic area of the BioE3 policy, whose full form is Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment.
accepted.tq: Link the policy acronym with its stated thematic priority rather than an unrelated sector.
